nodes.description: In thymoma-associated disease, abnormal T-cell selection and export of autoreactive T cells can support AChR autoimmunity. Tumor histology and immune changes vary; no single molecular lesion is asserted for every thymoma.

evidence.reference_title: Myasthenia gravis: the future is here.
evidence.snippet: Development of MG requires the generation of autoreactive T cells within the tumor and subsequent exit of these T cells to the periphery and is further associated with a reduction of Tregs

nodes.description: Assess and manage thymoma according to tumor stage and operability, generally with surgical removal when feasible. This oncological indication applies independently of MG severity or onset-age category; removal does not guarantee resolution of MG.

evidence.reference_title: Guideline for the management of myasthenic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Every MG patient must be evaluated for the presence of a thymoma. Thymomas must be surgically removed at any age regardless of the severity of myasthenia.

nodes.description: A complement-inhibitory macrocyclic peptide for AChR-positive generalized MG. It binds C5 and also impedes C5b–C6 interaction. Its mechanism does not make it appropriate for the predominant IgG4 MuSK pathway. Meningococcal vaccination and infection precautions remain necessary; these agents do not directly stop autoantibody production.

evidence.reference_title: Guideline for the management of myasthenic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Another complement factor 5 inhibitor is zilucoplan, which was successfully tested in a phase III RAISE trial in the indication MG.
